bun-cha-ca-nha-trang.name: Nha Trang fish-cake vermicelli soup
aliases: Nha Trang beam fish noodle soup
bun-cha-ca-nha-trang.serving_basis: Four bowls of clear fish broth with fish pieces, steamed and fried fish cakes, and fresh greens.
bun-cha-ca-nha-trang.description: Nha Trang fish-cake vermicelli is known for a clear, delicate broth made from sea-fish heads and bones, served with fish pieces and steamed or fried fish cakes. Bep Viet has edited a home-sized recipe, simmering gently and adding a measured amount of fermented shrimp paste to preserve the fish's natural sweetness.
bun-cha-ca-nha-trang.finished_dish: A bowl of clear, lightly fragrant fish broth with tender mackerel, springy fish cake, greens and a little lime and chili.
bun-cha-ca-nha-trang.serving: Blanch the noodles, arrange the mackerel and fish cakes in bowls, then ladle over the hot broth. Serve with fresh greens, banana blossom, lime and chili.
bun-cha-ca-nha-trang.image_alt: A bowl of Nha Trang fish-cake vermicelli soup with clear broth, mackerel, golden fish cakes and fresh greens.
bun-cha-ca-nha-trang.time_note: Use no pork bones; simmer the broth from marine fish heads and bones.
tips: Briefly blanch and rinse the fish bones to keep the broth clear and reduce fishy aromas.
Maintain a gentle simmer and avoid stirring the fish bones vigorously.
Add strained fermented shrimp paste gradually; saltiness and aroma vary by brand.

ingredients.name: Nha Trang fish cake
ingredients.notes: Use a mix of steamed and fried fish cakes, sliced.

ingredients.name: Onion
ingredients.notes: Char the surface lightly to bring out its aroma.

ingredients.name: Fermented fish sauce paste
ingredients.notes: Dissolve in water and strain out any sediment.

ingredients.name: Shredded banana blossom
ingredients.notes: Soak in diluted lime water and drain.

preparation_steps: Blanch the fish heads and bones for about 2 minutes, then rinse away foam and residue. Char the onion and ginger, and bruise the lemongrass.
Slice and pat dry the mackerel. Cut the fish cakes into bite-size pieces; wash the herbs and soak the banana blossom in diluted lemon water.
Mix the fermented shrimp paste with a little warm water, let it settle, then strain the clear liquid.
cooking_steps: Put the fish bones in a pot with water, onion, ginger, and lemongrass. Bring to a boil, skim, simmer gently for 35–40 minutes, then strain out the bones and aromatics.
Keep the strained broth at a gentle simmer. Poach the mackerel just until cooked and remove it; season with fish sauce, salt, rock sugar, and a little strained fermented shrimp paste at a time.
Briefly blanch the rice vermicelli and divide it among bowls. Add the mackerel and steamed and fried fish cakes, sprinkle with scallions, and ladle over hot broth.
Serve with fresh herbs, banana blossom, lime, and chili. Do not leave the cooked fish simmering, or it may turn mushy.

banh-can-da-lat.name: Da Lat mini rice cakes
aliases: Banh can with meatballs in Da Lat
banh-can-da-lat.serving_basis: Four servings of small rice cakes topped with egg and shrimp, served with tomato pork meatballs and shredded papaya.
banh-can-da-lat.description: Da Lat banh can are small rice-flour cakes cooked in individual clay molds until their edges turn crisp, traditionally served with dipping sauce, often tomato pork meatballs and shredded papaya. Bep Viet has adapted the dish for a home banh can pan or dimpled skillet, with quail egg and shrimp toppings.
banh-can-da-lat.finished_dish: Small cakes with crisp golden edges and soft egg-and-shrimp toppings, served with hot tomato pork meatballs and shredded papaya.
banh-can-da-lat.serving: Arrange the hot cakes on a plate and serve with tomato pork meatballs, shredded papaya and herbs. Dip each cake into the sauce before eating.
banh-can-da-lat.image_alt: Da Lat mini rice cakes topped with quail egg and shrimp, served with tomato pork meatballs and shredded papaya.
banh-can-da-lat.time_note: If using a cast-iron pan instead of a clay mold, adjust the heat so the cakes cook through before their edges become too dark.
tips: Rest the batter after mixing so the rice flour hydrates and the cakes cook evenly.
Preheat the molds before pouring in the batter; brush with only a thin film of oil for crisp edges.
Cook the pork meatballs through and keep the sauce hot for serving.
keywords: Banh can with meatballs in Da Lat

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Add gradually until the batter reaches a pourable consistency.

ingredients.name: Peeled fresh shrimp
ingredients.notes: Remove the vein and cut into small pieces.

ingredients.name: Ground pork
ingredients.notes: Choose pork shoulder with a little fat.

ingredients.name: Tomato
ingredients.notes: Finely chop for the xíu mại sauce.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: For seasoning the filling and sauce.

preparation_steps: Whisk the rice flour, tapioca starch, salt, and water until smooth. Rest for 15 minutes and whisk again. Chop the tomatoes, shallots, and scallions.
Mix the ground pork with half the shallots, a little fish sauce, and pepper; shape into small balls. Prepare the shrimp and crack the quail eggs into a small bowl.
Shred the papaya, soak in cold water for 5 minutes, then drain. Wash the fresh herbs.
cooking_steps: Sauté the remaining shallots until fragrant, then soften the tomatoes. Add water and the remaining fish sauce; bring to a boil, add the pork balls, and simmer for 12–15 minutes until the xíu mại are cooked through.
Heat the bánh căn mold and brush each well with a thin layer of oil. Fill each well about two-thirds full with batter, add quail egg or shrimp, and sprinkle with scallions.
Cover and cook for 4–6 minutes, until the tops set, the filling is cooked, and the edges are golden. Remove the cakes and repeat with the remaining batter.
Serve the hot cakes with tomato xíu mại, shredded papaya, and fresh herbs.

keywords: Banh can with meatballs in Da Lat

goi-cu-hu-dua-chay-ben-tre.name: Ben Tre vegan coconut-heart salad
aliases: Coconut tofu salad made from coconut
goi-cu-hu-dua-chay-ben-tre.serving_basis: Four plant-based servings of crisp coconut heart, tofu, tofu skin, Vietnamese coriander and peanuts.
goi-cu-hu-dua-chay-ben-tre.description: Coconut heart, the crisp, mildly sweet core of the palm, is closely associated with Ben Tre's coconut-growing region. This vegan salad combines it with tofu, tofu skin, Vietnamese coriander, peanuts and a sweet-sour dressing. Bep Viet uses soy sauce, lime and sugar instead of fish sauce to keep the dish fully plant-based.
goi-cu-hu-dua-chay-ben-tre.finished_dish: Crisp, cool coconut-heart strips pair with soft tofu, crunchy tofu skin, fragrant Vietnamese coriander and a gentle sweet-sour dressing.
goi-cu-hu-dua-chay-ben-tre.serving: Toss the salad shortly before serving. Plate it and top with peanuts, crisp tofu skin and vegan fried shallots. Serve any extra dressing on the side.
goi-cu-hu-dua-chay-ben-tre.image_alt: Ben Tre vegan coconut-heart salad with tofu, tofu skin, Vietnamese coriander and roasted peanuts.
goi-cu-hu-dua-chay-ben-tre.time_note: Choose soy sauce, tofu skin, and fried shallots made entirely from plant-based ingredients to keep the dish vegetarian.
tips: After slicing, soak the coconut heart in ice water with lime to preserve its pale color and crisp texture.
Dry the coconut heart and greens thoroughly before tossing so the salad does not become watery.
Check the tofu-skin and fried-shallot labels to ensure they contain no animal-derived additives.
keywords: Coconut tofu salad made from coconut

ingredients.name: Coconut heart
ingredients.notes: Slice into strips and soak in iced water with lime.

ingredients.name: Firm tofu
ingredients.notes: Fry until golden, cool, then slice into strips.

ingredients.name: Dried tofu skin
ingredients.notes: Soak until soft, pat dry, then fry until crisp.

ingredients.name: Shallots
ingredients.notes: Fry until crisp in vegetable oil.

preparation_steps: Thinly slice the coconut heart and immediately soak it in iced water with lime juice for about 10 minutes. Rinse briefly and drain very well.
Fry the tofu until evenly golden, cool, and slice into strips. Soak the tofu skin until soft, pat dry, and fry until crisp.
Slice the bell pepper, shred the carrot, and wash and chop the Vietnamese coriander. Roast and lightly crush the peanuts if needed; fry the shallots in vegetable oil.
cooking_steps: Stir together the soy sauce, lime juice, vinegar, sugar, chili, and a little water to make a sweet-and-sour dressing; taste and adjust.
Put the coconut heart, bell pepper, carrot, tofu, and Vietnamese coriander in a large bowl. Gradually add the dressing, toss gently, and let the flavors mingle for 3–5 minutes.
Arrange the salad on a plate and top with roasted peanuts, fried shallots, and crisp tofu skin. Serve immediately to preserve its crunch.

keywords: Coconut tofu salad made from coconut

goi-ga-mang-cut-lai-thieu.name: Lai Thieu chicken and mangosteen salad
goi-ga-mang-cut-lai-thieu.serving_basis: Four servings of shredded chicken salad with young mangosteen, onion, carrot, Vietnamese coriander, peanuts and sweet-sour fish sauce.
goi-ga-mang-cut-lai-thieu.description: Lai Thieu chicken and mangosteen salad is associated with the season for young mangosteen: firm chicken is tossed with crisp, mildly tart fruit, onion, Vietnamese coriander and peanuts. Bep Viet has edited a home-sized method, peeling the fruit under running water and soaking it in salted lime water to reduce sap and preserve its color.
goi-ga-mang-cut-lai-thieu.finished_dish: Tender shredded chicken, crisp mildly tart young mangosteen, cool vegetables, fragrant Vietnamese coriander and roasted peanuts.
goi-ga-mang-cut-lai-thieu.serving: Toss the salad just before serving and top with peanuts and fried shallots. Serve with prawn crackers or use the chicken broth to make a side porridge.
goi-ga-mang-cut-lai-thieu.image_alt: Lai Thieu chicken and mangosteen salad with shredded chicken, young mangosteen, Vietnamese coriander, carrot and peanuts.
goi-ga-mang-cut-lai-thieu.time_note: Green mangosteen is seasonal; 2 kg of whole fruit usually yields only about 400–500 g of edible flesh for the salad.
tips: Choose green or just-yellow mangosteens with firm flesh; ripe, soft fruit can break apart when tossed.
Wear gloves while peeling mangosteen under running water, then immediately soak the flesh in cold salted lime water to reduce sap and browning.
Poach the chicken until fully cooked, cool it promptly and refrigerate it if you will not toss the salad right away.
keywords: Lai Thieu chicken and mangosteen salad

ingredients.name: Young green mangosteen
ingredients.notes: Whole-fruit weight; yields about 400–500 g of flesh after peeling.

ingredients.name: Ginger
ingredients.notes: Bruise and use to poach the chicken.

ingredients.name: Lime juice
ingredients.notes: Divide between soaking the mangosteen and mixing the salad.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Divide between the poaching liquid and the mangosteen soak.

preparation_steps: Clean the chicken and simmer it gently in water with ginger until fully cooked. Remove and cool, then debone and shred into bite-size strands.

Wearing gloves to avoid the sap, peel the green mangosteen under running water. Separate the flesh, remove any large seeds, and immediately soak it in cold water with lime and a little salt; slice and keep chilled.
Thinly slice the onion, shred the carrot, and slice the cabbage. Wash and drain the Vietnamese coriander and basil. Mix the fish sauce with sugar, lime, garlic, and chili.
cooking_steps: Remove the mangosteen from its soaking water and drain thoroughly. Soak the onion in iced water for a few minutes, then gently squeeze to soften its sharpness.
Place the shredded chicken, mangosteen, onion, carrot, and cabbage in a large bowl. Add the dressing a little at a time and toss gently so the mangosteen slices stay intact.
Add the Vietnamese coriander, basil, and roasted peanuts; toss briefly. Taste for a balanced sweet, sour, and savory flavor.
Arrange the salad on a plate and top with roasted peanuts and fried shallots. Serve immediately; keep prepared ingredients chilled if not using them right away.

keywords: Lai Thieu chicken and mangosteen salad

nam-rom-kho-tieu-chay.name: Vegan straw mushrooms braised with pepper
aliases: Straw mushrooms braised with green pepper and vegetarian
nam-rom-kho-tieu-chay.serving_basis: Four servings of straw mushrooms braised with green peppercorns, served with rice and boiled vegetables.
nam-rom-kho-tieu-chay.description: Vegan straw mushrooms braised with pepper make a simple rice-table dish: plump mushrooms are simmered with soy sauce, green peppercorns and a little caramel until lightly glazed. Bep Viet has edited a fully plant-based version, using leek instead of shallot or garlic and omitting fish sauce.
nam-rom-kho-tieu-chay.finished_dish: Plump straw mushrooms in a lightly reduced soy glaze, warmly scented with green peppercorns and gently sweet.
nam-rom-kho-tieu-chay.serving: Serve hot with steamed rice and boiled greens. Add ground pepper or a few slices of chili for more heat.
nam-rom-kho-tieu-chay.image_alt: Vegan straw mushrooms braised with green peppercorns, chili and leek, served with steamed rice.
nam-rom-kho-tieu-chay.time_note: This is fully plant-based; use leek and check the caramel sauce and soy sauce ingredients if strict vegan preparation is required.
tips: Rinse the mushrooms quickly, drain them well and braise over medium heat so they do not release too much liquid.
Season with soy sauce first, then taste before adding salt because saltiness varies by brand.
Choose plant-based caramel coloring and soy sauce.

Straw mushrooms braised with green pepper

ingredients.name: Straw mushrooms
ingredients.notes: Trim the stems, rinse quickly and drain thoroughly.

ingredients.name: Leek
ingredients.notes: Slice and use in place of onion and garlic.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Add to make the braising sauce.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Add only after tasting the soy sauce.

preparation_steps: Trim the mushroom stems, rinse quickly under running water, and drain completely; halve larger mushrooms.
Rinse and lightly crush the green peppercorns. Slice the leek and chili; stir together the soy sauce, caramel sauce, sugar, and water.
cooking_steps: Heat the oil in a clay pot or heavy-based pan. Sauté the leek until fragrant, add the straw mushrooms, and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Pour the soy mixture into the pot, add the green peppercorns, and toss gently to coat the mushrooms. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat.
Braise for 8–10 minutes, until the sauce lightly thickens and coats the mushrooms. Taste and add salt if needed; finish with black pepper and chili.
Serve hot with steamed rice and boiled vegetables.
